title: Overview
text:
json outline schema (jos) is a standard way of expressing and storing the relationship between objects. it gives you simple linking data together to form an related concepts entitiesâtitle, author, description, flat list items that reference one another by parent id. haxcms uses jos as backbone for every sites site.json manifest: pages, their order, nesting, flexible metadata container downstream systems (like itself, praw) layer own conventions on top of.
this documentation covers three things:

  structure â core entity shape, how link tree.
 practical metadata.site, metadata.theme, metadata.platform, metadata.node groups defines jos.
 skeleton api http endpoints extends into reusable starter site templates ("skeletons") served over http.

new hax ecosystem? start with onboarding guide, which prerequisites, cloning repos, installing, running each project locally.

title: HAXcms Metadata Conventions
text:
json outline schema is intentionally flexible about metadata. in practice, haxcms uses stable metadata groups that are important to document for interoperability (including ingest into systems like praw), even though these not formally required by jos itself. 
  metadata.site
 holds site-level information and operational settings used haxcms:
 name â machine the site (folder / instance alignment).
 created updated unix timestamps.
 logo, domain, tags, homepageid common values.
 feature flags runtime behavior (for example lang, publishpageson, canonical, pathauto, sw, forceupgrade, gaid).
 git optional publishing/deployment information.
 


 metadata.theme
 describes active theme theme-level settings:
 element tag clean-one).
 path module (when present).
 variables visual tokens hexcode, cssvariable, icon, image, imagealt, imagelink.
 regions region-to-node mappings layouts.
 styleguide external style-guide url (if set, treats editing as external).
 metadata.platform (hax editor cms controls)
 stores audience, toggles, block-allow lists constrain audience currently novice or expert.
 features boolean map of platform capabilities addpage, deletepage, outlinedesigner, styleguide, insights, manifest, pagebreak, addblock, contentmap, viewsource, onlinesearch).
 allowedblocks array allowed html tags registered web-component names.
 current compatibility support also accepts legacy keys:
 delete mapped modern features.deletepage.
 blocks allowedblocks.

 block registration marks restricted when platformallows(tag) false.
 features.addblock = false prevents insertion ui actions.

 expert mode, an empty list defaults allowing all blocks; non-expert modes, access enforced metadata.node

 metadata.node.fields object storing node definitions related data.

title: Skeleton API
text:
the skeleton api builds on json outline schema to describe reusable starter "skeletons" for haxcms sites. a is document that combines: 
  high-level metadata about itself.
 initial site settings (name, description, theme).
 schemaâstyle of pages create.
 optional theme and visual dashboards uis.

skeleton documents are stored as files (for example in coreconfig/skeletons/), delivered over http via skeletonslist getskeleton endpoints â see endpoints.
a typical has this top-level structure:

{
 "meta": { /* */ },
 "site": site-level "build": {
 "type": "skeleton",
 "structure": "from-skeleton",
 "items": [ items ],
 "files": []
 "theme": "_skeleton": export from site-skeleton-generator }
}


 meta
 describes itself how it should appear uis:
 name â machine-readable key used file (and query value).
 description short what for.
 version definition.
 created iso 8601 timestamp when was created.
 type usually "skeleton".
 usecasetitle human-readable title shown selectors "online course").
 usecasedescription longer dashboards.
 usecaseimage path/url thumbnail image skeleton.
 category array strings grouping/filtering.
 tags describing attributes additional surface uis.
 


 site
 provides configuration:
 base (used folder/instance naming).
 default new site.
 identifier apply generated build
 defines generate skeleton. where directly schema:
 build type, structure strategy constructing "from-skeleton").
 closely match leaf/page structure.
 create or copy into each entry build.items typically has:
 id uuid/unique element.
 page display.
 slug uri portion resource (maps url).
 order ordering weight relative siblings.
 parent item (or null pages).
 indent indentation level (mirrors concept).
 content html seed page.
 arbitrary key/value data published, hideinmenu, tags).
 these can be thought an extended schema: they express same relationships while also providing richer per-page metadata.
 theme
 theme-specific by selection hexcode primary color hex code preview tiles.
 cssvariable css custom property reference color.

 non-required block currently workflows preserve source downstream systems:
 originalmetadata extracted groups, including site, platform, node, licensing information.
 originalsettings metadata.site.settings.
 fullthemeconfig expanded configuration snapshot.

title: Skeleton API HTTP Endpoints
text:
skeleton json documents (described in api) are exposed via two haxcms api endpoints, implemented both the php (operations::skeletonslist / operations::getskeleton) and node.js backends. 
  get /skeletonslist
 returns list of available skeletons visible to current user.
 query parameters
 user_token â required request token for active user (same used by other cms endpoints).
 response shape (success)
 {
 "status": 200,
 "data": [
 "title": "online course",
 "description": "an online course using clean one theme with syllabus lesson pages.",
 "image": "@haxtheweb/haxcms-elements/lib/theme-screenshots/theme-clean-one-thumb.jpg",
 "priority": 0,
 "category": ["course"],
 "attributes": [],
 "machinename": "online-course-clean-one",
 "machine-name": "demo-url": "#",
 "skeleton-url": ".../getskeleton?name=online-course-clean-one&user_token=..."
 }
 ]
}
 each item data is derived from corresponding files meta block. skeleton-url field provides a ready-to-use url fetching full getskeleton below. intentionally excludes internal fallback such as default-starter.
 


 /getskeleton
 definition single skeleton.
 name file key (usually meta.name value, without .json extension).
 "meta": { /* metadata */ },
 "site": site configuration "build": build instructions outline items "theme": visual "_skeleton": optional source snapshot }
}
 

if invalid or missing, endpoints return 403-style response. if named cannot be found, 404-style implementations search core definitions (for example coreconfig/skeletons) site-specific overrides _config/skeletons) when resolving file.
